FIG_AGGREGATE_SENSITIVITY_CAPTION: The aggregate reduction under alternative selections and weightings of the same five workloads. The published aggregate sums bytes, so each workload counts in proportion to its baseline size. Hollow markers fall below the target. All values are deterministic.
FIG_GPU_PROXY_SENSITIVITY_CAPTION: The GPU lab's allocation reduction recomputed from its requested buffer sizes, as a function of the assumed per-session delta. The open marker is the value hard-coded in the lab, which reproduces the published figure exactly and needs no GPU. No experiment in this repository measures that fraction.
FIG_HEAP_SCALING_CAPTION: Median V8 heap per session against the number of sessions, for each store design and workload. Panels use independent vertical scales, because the workloads differ in record size by more than an order of magnitude. The measuring host is reported in the Methods section.
FIG_HEAP_VS_JSON_CAPTION: Reduction relative to the duplicated store at 1,024 sessions: what serialized JSON predicts (open) and what a forced-collection read of the V8 heap shows (filled, median with percentile-bootstrap 95% interval over independent processes). Negative values mean a larger heap than the duplicated store.
FIG_KV_RESIDENCY_CAPTION: Key-value cache held live for 8 sessions of distilbert/distilgpt2 on MPS: 512 shared prefix tokens and 21 tokens per session, by three accountings. Sharing the prefix is predicted to save 84.1%; summed tensor sizes give 84.1% and the device allocator 84.4%.
FIG_LLM_PREFILL_CAPTION: Real forward passes: prefill time per turn when the whole prompt is processed again, and when a shared prefix's key-value tensors are reused so only the session's own tokens are processed. Labels give the speedup. Points are medians of per-trial medians, and their intervals describe repeatability within one process. Reusing a prefix is what a production prefix cache already does, so this compares against a baseline without one.
FIG_MATERIALIZATION_LATENCY_CAPTION: Time to turn one stored session back into its full request text, with each store's ratio to the duplicated store. Points are medians over independent processes, with percentile-bootstrap 95% intervals. Every condition reproduced the original text exactly. With a shared prompt, removing `structuredClone` from reconstruction moves the ratio from 1.69 to 1.06.
FIG_RHYME_CROSSOVER_CAPTION: JSON bytes for 40 same-shaped sessions as a growing share of them repeat one identical record. The rhyme stays nearly flat because it records every session; the exact-text cache improves with every duplicate. Reconstruction matched the original at every point. In-process bytes, not device memory.
FIG_SESSION_SCALING_CAPTION: Reduction in JSON bytes as the number of sessions sharing one system prompt grows, for four conversation lengths. Markers are measured on the real encoding; dashed lines are the closed form $R(n) = f(1 - 1/n)$, where $f$ is the shared fraction. The reduction saturates at $f$, and $f$ falls as sessions accumulate turns.
FIG_VENDOR_ARCHITECTURE_CAPTION: The product's layered architecture, reproduced unaltered from FractiAI's product kit. This is the vendor's marketing schematic, shown for orientation. Its adjectives (for example secure or observable) are not properties this study tests, and nothing in this figure is evidence.
FIG_WORKLOAD_REDUCTIONS_CAPTION: Representation-byte reduction for each registered workload, computed as one minus the Tiny Footprint form's UTF-8 JSON bytes over the conventional arm's. Diamonds show gzip applied to the same conventional JSON (zlib 1.2.12). Workload E is hatched because its working set covers one request and is not a lossless representation. These are serialized sizes, not resident memory.

| Claim | Evidence | Status |

| Aggregate representation reduction of 84.5%, clearing the 80% gate | Reproduced to every digit at 84.5%. 3 of 3 alternative aggregates fall below the gate: equal weight 74.3%, lossless only 77.0%, without the anti-pattern baseline 55.5%. | reproduced with a qualification |
| Sharing a system prompt across sessions uses less memory | At 1,024 sessions the live heap falls 32.8% against the JSON prediction of 49.5%. A plain object reference reaches 32.9% with no engine. | reproduced with a qualification |
| A rhyme stores about 31% less when sessions share a shape and differ in words | True of JSON bytes (31.1%). In the live heap at 1,024 sessions the shipped engine saves 4.2%, and a tighter encoding of the same idea 20.9%, against 20.1% for a plain reference. | reproduced with a qualification |
| An exact-text cache wins when every session repeats the same words | Reproduced: cache 198 bytes, rhyme 5,572 bytes. The cache is first smaller at 40% duplicates on the tested grid. | reproduced |
| Lower latency from reconstructing a working set | In process, materializing a session takes 1.69× and 11.81× the duplicated store's time for the two workloads, or 1.06× and 1.96× without cloning. | not reproduced |
| Real-model prefill speedup of 1.80× (historical, GTX 860M) | Direction reproduced on this host: 1.34× to 3.50× per turn. Decode alone 0.98× to 1.03×; prefill plus decode 1.06× to 1.63×. The tested mechanism is prefix reuse, which a prefix cache already provides. Logits match a full prefill to within 1.4e-4 on distilgpt2, where the check catches a cache built from the wrong prefix. On tiny-gpt2 it does not, so those turns show nothing. | reproduced with a qualification |
| Real-model train-step speedup of 1.17× (historical, GTX 860M) | Warmed up and with arms interleaved, this host gives 1.00× to 1.03×, with intervals spanning 0.94× to 1.09×. Both arms perform the same steps per round; the original lab ran one arm first with no warm-up. | not reproduced |
| GPU allocation falls 81.4%, from 288.00 to 53.60 MiB | Reproduced to every digit by arithmetic, with no GPU, because the value follows from requested buffer sizes and an assumed 15% delta. It is not a device reading, and no experiment here measures that assumption. | reproduced with a qualification |
| nvidia-smi peak falls 72.8%, from 313 to 85 MiB (historical, GTX 860M) | Needs NVIDIA hardware; the lab reports not_run on this host (nvcuda_unavailable). A real-model analogue is measured here: key-value residency 84.4% on the MPS allocator, 27.3% once weights are counted. | not testable on this host |
| Host-to-device turn materialization 9.60× faster (historical, GTX 860M) | Needs NVIDIA hardware. The copied payload alone is 9.41× smaller than the conventional one, so the byte count predicts most of the speedup recorded in the stored receipts (9.60×). | not testable on this host |
| A DRAM or accelerator memory reduction of 80% for AI serving | Not established by any receipt. Key-value residency alone can exceed that (84.4% here), but counting weights gives 27.3% here and 50.8% on the H100 roofline, and a prefix cache gets the same residency. | not reproduced |
| A four-pillar gate tells a holographic rhyme from a brick wall | It refuses a plain wall. The same bricks pass once they have a nested field and declare a nesting depth and a drift, because recursive and self_correcting read values the caller states. | reproduced with a qualification |
| On an H100, a rhyme holds 34.3% less KV memory than a prefix cache when wording differs (simulated) | Measured on distilgpt2, with 12.5% of tokens changed: 14.6% of KV cells repeat, and resuming from the other prompt's cache moves logits by 3.72. The simulation applies a JSON byte fraction of 38.9% to KV memory, and its equivalence check compares lengths. | not reproduced |
| Signature routing, context-fold hooks and an energy proxy | They run and pass: 3 comparisons against 15 for a scan, a fold ratio of 10.0% over 6 retained turns, and depth scaled from 8 to 1. These count comparisons, bytes and joules from assumed constants. None is a memory, latency or energy reading from a device. | reproduced with a qualification |
| `tiny benchmark` produces receipts on your machine | False before this work: on a host with no GPU it reported a stored laptop receipt as a fresh pass, naming that laptop as the device. Labs now report only what ran in the current invocation, and a regression test pins it. On this host the GPU lab's status is not_run and the suite's verdict is incomplete. | corrected in this repository |
